thread.title: Roku Stock Upgraded On Ad-Supported Streaming Video Growth |

author: PATRICK SEITZ
title: Roku Stock Upgraded On Ad-Supported Streaming Video Growth |
text:
Streaming video platform Roku ( ROKU ) is well positioned to benefit from the growth of advertiser-supported internet video, a Wall Street firm says. Roku stock received a bullish endorsement late Thursday from RBC Capital Markets.
X RBC analyst Mark Mahaney upgraded Roku stock to outperform from sector perform. He raised his price target on Roku stock to 70 from 48.
Roku stock initially jumped on the news. But it ended the regular session down 5.1% to 54.09 on the stock market today . It hit a record high of 77.57 on Oct. 1 before falling during the recent stock market correction .
"Long term, we view Roku as one of the best plays on ad-supported OTT (over-the-top)" internet video, Mahaney said in a report to clients.

Please contact customer service CLOSE Roku Stock: Booming Advertising Business Roku is best known for selling set-top boxes and dongles for accessing internet video services such as Netflix ( NFLX ) and Hulu. It competes in that space with Amazon.com ( AMZN ), Apple ( AAPL ), Alphabet 's ( GOOGL ) Google and others. Roku also licenses a smart TV operating system to television makers such as TCL, Hisense, RCA and Sharp.
But Roku makes most of its money selling advertising through its platform for its Roku Channel and third-party, ad-supported internet video channels.
As of the June quarter , it had 22 million active user accounts, up 46% year over year.
"We believe there is convincing evidence that Roku can sustain very high platform revenue growth rates for several years," Mahaney said. Its platform revenue rose 96% year over year to $90.3 million in the second quarter.
Netflix Stock Gets Another Price-Target Hike Elsewhere in the streaming video segment, Netflix stock earned another price-target hike following its third-quarter report.
Oppenheimer reiterated its outperform rating on Netflix and upped its price target to 410 from 370. It slid 4.1% to 332.67 on Friday.
"Netflix continues to build a bigger moat as the majority of (its) content spend is through its internal studio, which protects the company from media consolidation and forthcoming OTT services," Oppenheimer analyst Jason Helfstein said in his note to clients.
Netflix stock received nearly 20 price-target increases from Wall Street analysts after its third-quarter report.
